newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - French ADRs fall on election worries.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - French ADRs fall on election worries.

text.p: American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) in French companies mostly fell Wednesday on jitters about a possible left-wing election win, traders said.
"The thing that is driving the ADR market is the French stocks, simply because of the massive correction that they've had," a trader said.
The Paris exchange's benchmark CAC-40 index fell as much as 4.4 percent before recovering to close down 3.6 percent. French blue chip ADRs followed suit.
Investors were worried about prospects that the opposition Socialists could take over parliament in runoff elections Sunday.
Oil company Total SA fell 1-1/4 to 46-1/2 in volume that by late morning was almost four times daily trade. Fellow oil giant Elf Aquitaine dropped 2-5/8 to 50-1/2, also in heavy trade.
Alcatel Alsthom Cie Generale d'Electricite' was off 1-3/8 at 22-1/4. Luxury goods maker LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton fell 7/8 to 48-5/8 and pharmaceutical company Rhone-Poulenc fell 7/8 to 32.
The jitters hit other European ADRs, particularly Spanish issues. Oil company Repsol fell 1-1/4 to 42-5/8 and Telefonica de Espana was off 1-1/4 at 92-5/8.
Among other European stocks, Swedish telecommunications equipment maker Telefon AB L.M Ericsson was up 1/8 to 36. Volume was heavy and Ericsson was the most-active ADR.
Ericsson had eased at its opening on concerns that a possible merger between AT&T Corp and SBC Communications Inc could mean it would lose customers.
"Ericsson is always active," a trader said. "Ericsson is a supplier, and where would they be with that merger?"
Canadian telecommunications equipment company Newbridge Networks Corp rose 7/8 to a 12-month high of 42-5/8 after Alex. Brown raised its rating to strong buy from buy.
Among Latin American stocks, Brazilian telephone company Telebras SA rose 1-1/4 to 135-7/8.
Decliners led advancers 229 to 224 among 814 ADRs. The ADR group rose 0.12 percent and volume in late morning was 36.5 million ADRs.
ADRs allow U.S. trading of foreign shares.
